title: 10 Must-Do NFL Trades: Derrick Henry to Patriots, Budda Baker to Bills & More Picks
body:
The NFL’s trade deadline looms on Tuesday, and speculation is already swirling around the league’s biggest contenders. While a flurry of deals has already reshaped rosters – Seattle added veteran guard Quenton Nelson and San Francisco bolstered its secondary – analysts say the window for bold, deadline‑day moves is still wide open. From a potential reunion between Kirk Cousins and the Minnesota Vikings to a blockbuster swap that could land Derrick Henry in New England, the next 48 hours could dramatically alter the playoff picture.

One of the most talked‑about scenarios involves the New England Patriots, who have struggled to establish a consistent ground game since the departure of Damien Harris. Adding a power back like Henry would give Bill Belichick a proven workhorse capable of grinding out yards against even the toughest defensive fronts. In return, New England could part with a combination of draft capital and a depth receiver, giving the Patriots a chance to finally pair a dominant run game with their already potent passing attack. While the price may be steep, the upside – a balanced offense that can control the clock in the postseason – is hard to ignore.

Across the country, the Minnesota Vikings are rumored to be courting former quarterback Kirk Cousins for a second stint. Cousins, who spent the first five seasons of his career in Minnesota before moving on to Washington and then the Dallas Cowboys, still enjoys a strong rapport with the organization’s front office and fan base. A return could provide the Vikings with a reliable veteran presence while they continue to develop rookie quarterback J.J. McCarthy. The trade would likely involve a mid‑round draft pick and perhaps a defensive player to sweeten the deal, but the familiarity factor and immediate upgrade at the position could outweigh the cost.

In the AFC East, the Buffalo Bills have been linked to a possible acquisition of safety Budda Baker from the Arizona Cardinals. Baker’s versatility – capable of covering tight ends, slot receivers, and running backs – would give Buffalo a more dynamic secondary, complementing the Bills’ already formidable pass rush. Arizona, on the other hand, could look to recoup Baker’s value with a combination of draft picks and a young defensive prospect, allowing the Cardinals to continue rebuilding around quarterback Kyler Murray. The move would also address Buffalo’s recent struggles in the secondary against high‑powered offenses, a weakness that could be exposed in a potential AFC championship run.

Meanwhile, the Las Vegas Raiders have been identified as a possible landing spot for wide receiver George Pickens, whose big‑play ability could finally give the team a true deep threat. Pickens, a second‑round pick out of Pittsburgh, has shown flashes of brilliance but has been hampered by inconsistent quarterback play in Pittsburgh. A trade to Vegas, where quarterback Jimmy Garoppolo is looking to reestablish himself as a starter, could provide both parties with the missing pieces they need. The Raiders would likely need to part with a mid‑level pick and a rotational defender, but the upside of adding a dynamic playmaker to a developing offense is compelling.

These speculative moves underscore a broader trend: teams that are on the cusp of the playoffs are increasingly willing to sacrifice future assets for immediate impact. The NFL’s salary‑cap structure and the limited number of high‑value players mean that any trade must be carefully balanced against long‑term roster health. As the deadline approaches, front offices will be weighing the risk of missing out on a potential champion‑caliber addition against the cost of depleting draft capital that could sustain success for years to come.

Looking ahead, the final day of trading will likely separate the bold from the cautious. If the Patriots secure Henry, the Vikings bring back Cousins, and the Bills lock up Baker, the AFC landscape could shift dramatically before the regular season concludes. Conversely, teams that choose to stand pat may find themselves scrambling in the postseason against opponents who made decisive moves. With only two days left, the league’s most ambitious franchises have a narrow window to reshape their destinies – and the outcomes of those decisions will echo throughout the playoffs.
